research_material:

winner.text: Your rice is mushy. Here's why (and how to fix it).
winner.reasoning: This immediately validates their frustration (most beginners have failed at rice) while promising a solution they can act on. For someone who just moved out and is probably embarrassed about kitchen failures, this warm acknowledgment builds trust before the carousel even starts.

runner_up.text: Your first apartment dinner just got way easier.
runner_up.reasoning: Directly speaks to their life stage and removes intimidation with a reassuring tone. Safe, on-brand, and specifically resonates with the 'just moved out' audience without requiring them to have already failed.

script.script:
[HOOK - 0-3 sec]
"Your rice is mushy. Here's why (and how to fix it)."
[PAUSE]

[PROBLEM]
"You're probably using too much water. Most beginners do—it's the #1 reason rice turns into porridge."
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Too much water = mushy rice]
[CUT]

[VALUE]
"Here's the fix: use a 1-to-1 ratio. One cup of rice to one cup of water. Bring it to a boil, then lower the heat and cover it. Let it sit for 15 minutes without peeking."
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: 1 cup rice : 1 cup water]
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Low heat + lid + 15 min]
[PAUSE]

"That's it. You'll get fluffy, separate grains every time."
[CUT]

[CTA]
"Save this for your next grocery run—and make rice that actually tastes like rice."
script.viewer_takeaway: Learn the exact water-to-rice ratio and simple steps to make perfectly fluffy rice instead of mushy rice.

cover_options: Close-up of a spoon breaking through mushy rice with bold text 'Your Rice Is Mushy' overlaid in warm sans-serif font
Split-screen: left side shows mushy rice in bowl, right side shows fluffy rice with checkmark, text 'Fix Mushy Rice' centered

frame_plan.on_screen_text: Your rice is mushy. Here's why.
frame_plan.visual_direction: Close-up of spoon sinking into mushy rice; warm, kitchen lighting; text appears with gentle emphasis
Split view: measuring cup pouring excess water over rice on left; sad/concerned emoji or visual cue on right
Hands holding an oversized water measuring cup next to standard rice cup; warm voiceover tone, relatable imagery
Two measuring cups side-by-side with rice and water, clearly marked and equal; bright, clear lighting

frame_plan.on_screen_text: Boil, lower heat, cover, wait 15 min
frame_plan.visual_direction: Sequence of 4 small visuals: pot boiling → flame lowering → lid closing → timer at 15 minutes
Close-up of perfect, fluffy rice being fluffed with fork; warm golden lighting; satisfied expression or thumbs up
Hands saving post to phone/bookmark gesture; finished rice bowl in soft focus background; encouraging, warm tone

assets_needed: Two measuring cups (1 cup each) with rice and water
Pot on stovetop at boiling stage
Pot with lid being placed on top
Kitchen timer or clock showing 15 minutes
Final finished rice in serving bowl (warm, natural lighting)
On-screen text graphics (warm sans-serif, cream/warm white on subtle background)
B-roll of hands throughout for continuity
Warm color grade/filter (golden hour vibes, no harsh lighting)

justifications.clarity: Hook + problem identified by 3 seconds; 1:1 ratio is concrete and instantly understandable.
justifications.retention: Solution arrives quickly but no dramatic tension or before-after payoff to keep eyes locked past slide 3.
justifications.save_potential: Practical, reusable formula with clear steps makes this a genuine reference post for beginners.
justifications.shareability: Solves a relatable problem but lacks the 'wow' factor or humor that drives tagging friends in comments.
justifications.audience_fit: First-time kitchen failure (mushy rice) is a documented beginner pain point; tone is warm and non-judgmental.
justifications.cta_strength: Save request is natural and tied to use case; 'for your next grocery run' adds specificity without friction.

weaknesses.issue: Retention dip mid-video: solution delivery is clean but lacks a hook moment to sustain engagement between problem statement and payoff.
weaknesses.fix: Add a 1-second reaction moment on Slide 3—rewrite to: 'The good news? It's a one-minute fix. One cup of rice. One cup of water. That's literally it.' This creates a mini surprise beat before the ratio reveal.

weaknesses.issue: Shareability is underutilized: the post solves a problem but doesn't give viewers a reason to tag someone or spark conversation.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite Slide 6 caption to: 'If your rice ever looks like this, you're doing it right. Tag someone who needs to see this.' This converts a solo learning moment into a social moment.

weaknesses.issue: Visual repetition risk: Slides 4–5 show measuring cups and stovetop sequences that may feel instructional-video generic rather than Instagram-native.
weaknesses.fix: On Slide 5, instead of static burner flame imagery, use a quick POV hand-cam of someone actually lowering the flame—adds motion energy and relatability over sterile demonstration visuals.

captions: Your rice is mushy. Here's why—and how to fix it in literally one minute. 1:1 ratio, low heat, 15 min, done. No more porridge. Save this before your next trip to the store. 🍚
If your rice looks like this, you're using too much water. The fix? 1 cup rice : 1 cup water. Boil. Lower heat. Cover. Walk away for 15 minutes. Fluffy rice guaranteed. Save this. 📌
growth.final_call_reason: Core mechanics are solid (clarity 9, audience fit 9) with a practical, save-worthy formula; weaknesses are engagement-layer issues that won't tank performance but a 1-second reaction beat and tagability line would push it from good to strong.
